Fill each tortilla with chicken, roll it up and set it in the dish. Cover with the remaining sauce and scatter on the torn mozzarella.
Bake for 15–20 minutes, until bubbling and lightly browned. Finish with the remaining spring onions.

title: Beef and bean fideo loco
steps: Snap the spaghetti into short lengths. Heat half the oil in a deep pan and toast the pasta until lightly golden. Scoop it out.
Add the remaining oil and brown the beef, breaking it up with a spoon.
Dice the onion and stir it into the beef for 5 minutes. Add crushed garlic and cumin and stir until fragrant.
Pour in the passata and stock and return the toasted pasta to the pan.
Simmer until the pasta is soft, then stir in the rinsed pinto beans and warm them through.
Serve in bowls with plenty of red broth and a small handful of chopped coriander.

title: Beef taco salad
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Slice the tortillas into thin strips and toss with half the oil.
Bake the strips in a single layer for 8–10 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Fry the beef in the remaining oil. Add cumin and paprika, breaking up the mince until it is cooked through.
Chop the lettuce and tomatoes. Drain the sweetcorn, grate the cheddar and mix the salsa with juice from one lime.
Heap the lettuce and tomatoes into bowls, top with beef and sweetcorn and spoon over the dressing.
Scatter the cheddar and tortilla strips on top. Serve with the remaining lime cut into wedges.

title: Korean fried chicken
steps: Cut the chicken into even bites and pat them dry. Whisk the egg in a bowl and spread the cornflour on a plate.
Dip the chicken pieces in egg and coat all over in cornflour. Shake off loose flour.
Heat most of the oil in a frying pan. Fry in small batches until cooked to 74°C (165°F), then transfer to a rack.
Heat the rest of the oil and briefly fry the cooked chicken again until the coating turns extra crisp.
In a small pan, stir together the gochujang, honey, soy, vinegar and grated ginger. Bubble for a minute.
Toss the chicken in the glaze just before serving and scatter over sesame and sliced spring onions.

title: Orange chicken
steps: Rinse the rice and cook following the packet. Finely cut a few strips of orange zest and juice both oranges.
Mix the juice with soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, ginger, garlic and a teaspoon of cornflour.
Dice the chicken, toss it in beaten egg and coat in the remaining cornflour.
Fry the chicken in the hot oil in batches until crisp and 74°C (165°F) at the centre. Transfer to a rack.
Tip off the excess oil. Add the juice mixture and orange zest to the pan and bring to a bubble until it turns glossy.
Toss the chicken in the thick glaze and immediately serve alongside the rice.

title: Chicken pad see ew
steps: Soften the wide noodles according to the packet, then drain them very well. Thinly slice the chicken and cut the broccoli into small florets.
Mix the soy, fish sauce, sugar and vinegar. Crush the garlic.
Heat half the oil in a wide pan and fry the chicken until fully cooked, then briefly stir-fry the broccoli and garlic.
Push the chicken and broccoli aside. Add the beaten eggs to the empty space and stir into loose curds.
Add the remaining oil, sauce and noodles. Let the underside of the noodles catch against the hot pan for a minute before tossing.
Toss until the noodles are dark and glossy and the egg and chicken are evenly mixed through. Serve hot.

title: Chinese pepper steak
steps: Cook the rice following the packet. Slice the beef into thin strips across the grain.
Cut the peppers and onion into thick strips. Stir the soy, ginger, garlic, cornflour, pepper, sugar and vinegar into 100 ml water.
Heat half the oil in a wide frying pan and brown the beef quickly in batches. Transfer to a clean plate.
Add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the peppers and onion until browned at the edges.
Return the beef to the pan. Stir up the sauce, pour it in and cook until it thickens and the beef is cooked to your liking.
Divide the plain rice between bowls and spoon the steak and peppers beside it.

title: Honey garlic prawn stir-fry
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it following the packet. Cut the broccoli and pepper into bite-size pieces.
Whisk the honey, soy, vinegar, cornflour and crushed garlic with 60 ml water.
Pat the prawns dry. Heat half the oil in a pan and cook the prawns until pink and opaque. Lift them onto a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the broccoli and pepper for a few minutes. Add the peas and a splash of water.
Pour in the sauce and bubble until it coats the vegetables. Return the prawns and toss until glossy and hot.
Spoon the stir-fry and its sauce over the rice.

title: Korean BBQ meatball rice bowls
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Set the rice cooking following the packet.
Mix the beef, egg, breadcrumbs, crushed garlic, grated ginger and half the soy. Form 16 small meatballs.
Spread on a lined tray and roast for 14–17 minutes, until cooked to 71°C (160°F).
Slice the cucumber and toss with half the vinegar. Heat the gochujang, honey, sesame oil, remaining soy and vinegar in a pan.
Bubble until lightly syrupy, then roll the roasted meatballs in the glaze.
Serve the glazed meatballs over rice with cucumber slices and a sprinkling of sesame seeds.

title: Steak rice bowls with spicy mayo
steps: Cook and fluff the rice. Cut the carrots into fine matchsticks and slice the spring onions.
Toss the carrots in half the lime juice. Stir the other half into the mayo with sriracha.
Pat the steak dry, season it with salt and heat the oil in a heavy frying pan.
Sear the steak on both sides to at least 63°C (145°F), then rest for at least 3 minutes.
Slice across the grain and toss the meat with its juices and the soy sauce.
Divide the rice, steak and carrots into bowls. Drizzle over the spicy mayo and add spring onions.

title: Chicken rice paper bites
steps: Dice the chicken finely, shred the cabbage and grate the ginger. Slice the spring onions.
Fry the chicken in a little vegetable oil until it reaches 74°C (165°F). Stir in cabbage, ginger, onions and half the soy and cook until dry enough to mound.
Let the filling cool on a clean plate. Dip a sheet of rice paper into water briefly and lay it flat.
Put two spoonfuls of filling in the middle. Fold each side over, then fold the ends tight to form a parcel. Repeat.
Heat the remaining oil and fry the parcels in batches, leaving space between them, until golden on both sides.
Mix the remaining soy with vinegar and sesame oil. Serve alongside the bites for dipping.

title: Bang bang chicken bowls
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Rinse the rice and put it on to cook.
Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and coat in beaten egg, then breadcrumbs.
Spread the chicken on a lined tray and brush lightly with oil. Bake for 14–18 minutes, turning once, until crisp and 74°C (165°F).
Mix the mayo, sweet chilli sauce and sriracha until pale pink. Shred the cabbage and slice the cucumber and spring onions.
Toss the hot crispy chicken with just enough sauce to lightly coat each bite.
Pile the chicken over rice with the cabbage and cucumber. Add spring onions and serve with the remaining sauce.

title: Sweet and sour pork with pineapple
steps: Rinse and cook the rice. Cube the pork and slice the peppers into squares.
Whisk ketchup, vinegar, soy, sugar, a teaspoon of cornflour and 100 ml water into a sauce.
Toss the pork in the remaining cornflour. Fry in hot oil until browned all over and 63°C (145°F) inside.
Move the pork to a clean plate to rest for at least 3 minutes. Stir-fry the peppers for 3 minutes.
Add the drained pineapple and the sauce. Bubble until thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Return the pork to the pan, toss to coat and serve over the rice.

title: Cajun prawn Alfredo
steps: Boil the fettuccine until just firm, then drain it, keeping a cup of the cooking water.
Pat the prawns dry and toss with paprika, oregano, chilli and pepper.
Heat half the butter and fry the prawns until pink and opaque. Lift them onto a clean plate.
Melt the rest of the butter in the same pan and cook the garlic for 30 seconds. Add the cream and stir up the browned seasoning.
Toss in the pasta with some cooking water and grated parmesan. Return the prawns and warm through.
Finish with lemon juice and chopped parsley.

title: Beef meatballs with creamy parmesan orzo
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Mix beef, beaten egg, breadcrumbs, herbs, half the garlic and salt.
Roll into 16 meatballs and bake on a lined tray until browned and 71°C (160°F) at the centre.
Melt the butter in a saucepan and stir in the remaining garlic. Add the orzo and toast briefly.
Pour in the stock and simmer, stirring every few minutes until the orzo is tender and creamy.
Stir in most of the grated parmesan off the heat. Loosen with a splash of hot water if needed.
Spoon the orzo into bowls, add the browned meatballs and finish with the remaining parmesan, cracked pepper and parsley.

title: Prawn and vegetable yakisoba
steps: Cook the noodles a minute short of the packet timing and drain well. Slice the cabbage and carrot thinly.
Mix soy, Worcestershire sauce, ketchup and sugar. Finely grate the ginger.
Fry the prawns in half the oil until pink and opaque. Lift them onto a clean plate.
Add the remaining oil, ginger, cabbage and carrot. Stir-fry until the vegetables soften slightly.
Add noodles and sauce. Let the noodles sit for a minute to develop browned edges, then toss with the prawns.
Serve immediately with plenty of finely sliced spring onions.

title: New Orleans BBQ prawns with bread
steps: Slice the bread into generous pieces. Pat the prawns dry and mince the garlic.
Melt a little of the butter in a wide pan. Stir in garlic, paprika and pepper until fragrant.
Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, hot sauce and lemon juice. Bubble until reduced a little.
Add the prawns and simmer gently, turning once, until pink and opaque.
Take the pan off the heat and whisk in the remaining cold butter a piece at a time. Stir in chopped parsley.
Divide the prawns and peppery sauce into bowls with slices of bread for dipping.

title: Chicken-fried chicken with milk gravy
steps: Peel and cube the potatoes. Boil until soft and add the peas to a separate pan for their last few minutes.
Slice the chicken into four even cutlets. Reserve 2 tablespoons of flour for the gravy and mix the rest with garlic powder, half the salt and half the pepper.
Beat the eggs with a little of the milk. Coat the cutlets in the flour, then egg and then flour again to make a craggy coating.
Fry in hot oil until golden and 74°C (165°F) in the centre. Rest on a rack and carefully pour off most of the oil.
Whisk the reserved flour into the drippings, then slowly add most of the remaining milk. Simmer until it coats a spoon and add the remaining pepper.
Mash the potatoes with butter, salt and the last splash of milk. Put the chicken beside the mash and peas and spoon its gravy over one end.

title: Minced beef and gravy with mash
steps: Peel the potatoes and cut into chunks. Boil for about 15 minutes until soft.
While they cook, brown the mince in a wide pan, breaking it up. Add thinly sliced onion and cook until softened.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for a minute. Pour in the stock gradually and add the Worcestershire sauce and pepper.
Simmer for 8–10 minutes until the gravy is thick and the mince is cooked through.
Drain the potatoes and mash with milk, butter and salt. Boil the peas in a small pan and drain.
Heap the mince and onion gravy over the mash and serve the peas alongside.

title: Chicken Caesar pasta salad
steps: Cook the rigatoni, drain and rinse briefly under cold water. Shake it dry.
Slice the chicken into cutlets. Fry in half the oil until golden and 74°C (165°F) inside, then let it cool before slicing.
Cube the sourdough and toast it in the remaining oil. Chop the lettuce and shave the parmesan.
Whisk the yoghurt, mayonnaise, mustard, Worcestershire, lemon juice and pepper into a thick dressing.
Toss the pasta, chicken and lettuce with the dressing. Add the parmesan and croutons just before serving.

title: Creamy chicken and green chile pasta bake
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Halve and deseed the poblanos and roast cut-side down for 15 minutes.
Cook the penne until just underdone. Slice the poblanos and dice the chicken.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and cook the chicken to 74°C (165°F). Add crushed garlic, cumin and salt.
Stir in the cream cheese and milk over low heat. Fold through the drained pasta, sliced poblanos and half the grated cheddar.
Spoon into a baking dish and scatter with the rest of the cheese. Bake for 15 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Scatter thinly sliced spring onions over the bake and rest for 3 minutes before serving.

title: Buffalo chicken sliders
steps: Gently simmer the chicken in water until the middle reaches 74°C (165°F).
Finely shred the cabbage and toss it with mayonnaise, vinegar and half the salt.
Warm the butter, hot sauce, honey and the rest of the salt in a saucepan until combined.
Drain the chicken and shred it with two forks. Toss it in the warm Buffalo sauce.
Split and toast the buns in a dry frying pan.
Load the buns with the saucy shredded chicken and a small heap of the dressed cabbage.

title: Gochujang coconut chicken with rice
steps: Rinse the rice and set it cooking. Dice the onion and cut the chicken into bite-size pieces.
Brown the chicken in the hot oil, then stir in the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the grated garlic, ginger and gochujang and cook briefly while stirring.
Pour in coconut milk. Simmer until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the sauce lightly coats a spoon.
Squeeze in lime juice and fluff the cooked rice.
Spoon the coconut chicken beside the rice and finish with spring onions and sesame seeds.

title: Turkey and mango salad with soy and lime
steps: Thinly slice the turkey. Toss with half the soy sauce and the grated ginger.
Heat the vegetable oil in a hot pan. Sear the turkey strips until browned and 74°C (165°F) at the centre.
Cut the mango into chunks, slice the cucumber, finely shred the red cabbage and slice the spring onions.
Whisk the remaining soy with juice from one lime, sesame oil and honey.
Toss the salad in the dressing. Add the warm or cooled turkey and spring onions, then serve with wedges of the second lime.

title: Creamy chicken casserole with cracker topping
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Poach the chicken in gently simmering water until it reaches 74°C (165°F), then shred it.
Melt most of the butter in a saucepan and stir in the flour and thyme. Cook for a minute.
Gradually whisk in the milk and stock. Simmer until smooth and thick, then stir in the cream cheese and pepper.
Fold the chicken and frozen peas into the sauce. Pour into a shallow baking dish.
Crush the crackers roughly and toss with the rest of the melted butter. Scatter across the casserole.
Bake for 18–20 minutes until it is hot at the centre and the cracker crumbs turn golden.

title: Sticky five-spice chicken
steps: Cook the rice following the packet. Pat the chicken thighs dry, leaving them whole.
Mix soy, honey, five-spice, garlic, ginger and vinegar with 50 ml water.
Heat the oil in a wide frying pan and brown the chicken on both sides.
Add the sauce and cover to cook the chicken through. Remove the lid and simmer until the glaze thickens and the meat reaches 74°C (165°F).
Quarter the pak choi and steam over boiling water for 3 minutes, until just tender.
Serve the chicken, pak choi and rice together. Spoon over the glaze and add sliced spring onions.

title: Vietnamese chicken and cabbage salad
steps: Poach the chicken gently until the middle reaches 74°C (165°F). Let it cool slightly and pull it into shreds.
Finely shred both kinds of cabbage and cut the carrot into thin matchsticks. Tear the mint leaves.
Toast the peanuts in a dry frying pan and crush them roughly.
Whisk juice from two limes with fish sauce, vinegar, sugar and crushed garlic.
Toss the shredded chicken and vegetables with the dressing and mint. Scatter with peanuts and serve with the remaining lime in wedges.

title: Chicken, salami and pepperoncini salad
steps: Slice the chicken into cutlets and fry in a little of the olive oil until golden and 74°C (165°F) at the centre.
Chop the lettuce and halve the tomatoes. Dice the salami and thinly slice the drained peppers.
Whisk the rest of the oil with vinegar, mustard, oregano and pepper.
Let the cooked chicken rest for a few minutes, then cut it into bite-size pieces.
Toss the vegetables, chicken, salami and peppers with enough dressing to lightly coat each bite.

title: Salmon-stuffed cucumber boats
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Rub the salmon with oil and roast until it flakes and reaches 63°C (145°F).
Cool the salmon, remove any skin and flake it into a bowl. Slice the spring onions thinly.
Mix the yoghurt, mayo, mustard, lemon juice and half the spring onions. Fold through the salmon without breaking every piece.
Halve the cucumbers lengthwise and scoop out the soft seeds with a spoon to make boats.
Mound the salmon filling into the cucumbers and finish with black pepper and the remaining spring onions.

title: Chicken summer rolls with sriracha dip
steps: Gently poach the chicken in water until it reaches 74°C (165°F). Let it cool, then shred it.
Very finely slice the red cabbage, cut the carrots into matchsticks and pick the mint leaves.
Mix the yoghurt, mayo, sriracha and lime juice into a smooth dip.
Dip a rice paper sheet briefly in water. Put the chicken, cabbage, carrot and two mint leaves in the middle.
Fold in both sides and roll snugly. Repeat and cut each roll in half on the diagonal. Serve with the dip.

title: Sheet-pan beef kebabs
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) and line a tray. Cut the steak and peppers into even chunks and the onions into wedges.
Toss the beef and vegetables with oil, crushed garlic, paprika, cumin, lemon zest and salt.
Thread the beef, pepper and onion onto metal skewers and arrange on the tray.
Roast for about 10–13 minutes, turning once, until browned and the beef reaches at least 63°C (145°F). Rest for 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, cover the couscous with boiling water according to the packet. Fluff it with a fork and add chopped parsley and lemon juice.
Serve the skewers beside a mound of couscous.

title: Creamy curry chicken pasta
steps: Cook the penne until firm at the centre, keeping a cup of the cooking water when you drain it.
Thinly slice the chicken and chop the onion. Fry the chicken in the hot oil until coloured on both sides.
Add the onion and crushed garlic and cook until soft. Stir through the curry powder for 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock and cream. Simmer until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the sauce thickens.
Add the peas and penne and cook for a few minutes, adding a splash of pasta water to loosen the sauce.
Finish with lemon juice and chopped coriander.

title: Turkey cheeseburgers
steps: Mix the turkey with garlic powder, salt and pepper, and shape it into four patties without packing it tightly.
Tear the lettuce leaves, thickly slice the tomatoes and cut the cheese into thin slices.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the patties on each side until brown and 74°C (165°F) in the middle.
Lay cheese on each patty, cover the pan for a minute and let it melt.
Toast the split buns and stir the mustard into the mayonnaise.
Spread sauce on each bun and build with lettuce, tomato and a turkey cheeseburger patty.

title: Crispy lemon chicken cutlets
steps: Split the chicken breasts horizontally and pound the pieces lightly so they are an even thickness. Trim the beans.
Mix flour with salt and pepper on a plate. Beat the egg in a bowl, then mix lemon zest through the breadcrumbs on another plate.
Coat each cutlet with flour, egg and breadcrumbs. Fry in hot oil until crisp and the centre reaches 74°C (165°F).
Cook the beans in boiling water for a few minutes and drain. Toss with butter and crushed garlic in the warm pan.
Drain the chicken on a rack so the crust stays crisp. Cut the remaining lemon into thin rounds.
Serve the cutlets beside the green beans with the lemon rounds for squeezing.

title: Turkey and carrot pilaf
steps: Toast the flaked almonds in a dry lidded pan, then set them aside. Rinse the rice and grate the carrots coarsely.
Dice the turkey and onion. Heat the oil and brown the turkey, then add the onion for 4 minutes.
Add the cumin, turmeric, carrot and rice. Stir until the rice is coated with oil and spices.
Pour in the stock and bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, until the rice is tender and the turkey reaches 74°C (165°F).
Rest covered for 4 minutes, then fluff the grains gently with a fork.
Fold in chopped parsley and lemon juice. Scatter the toasted almonds over each bowl.

title: Korean-style beef kebab tortillas
steps: Slice the beef into bite-size pieces. Mix soy, gochujang, honey, crushed garlic and grated ginger, then coat the meat.
Shred the cabbage and cut the cucumber into sticks. Dress with vinegar and sesame oil.
Thread the beef onto metal skewers. Heat a griddle pan and brush it lightly with vegetable oil.
Griddle on all sides, until browned and at least 63°C (145°F) in the centre. Rest for 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan. Slide the beef off the skewers.
Fill each tortilla with beef, cabbage and cucumber, and finish with sesame seeds.

title: Spicy peanut chicken noodles
steps: Cook the noodles according to the packet. Scoop out a mug of cooking water before draining.
Whisk the peanut butter, sriracha, soy and lime juice with about 100 ml of the hot noodle water.
Slice the chicken into even cutlets. Slice the pepper and cut the carrot into matchsticks.
Sear the chicken cutlets until the centre reaches 74°C (165°F) and lift onto a clean board. Add the pepper and carrot and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles and peanut sauce and toss briefly, loosening with more cooking water if needed.
Slice the cooked chicken and lay it over the sauced noodles. Top with chopped peanuts and finely sliced spring onions.

title: Barbecue chicken and pineapple toast
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Poach the chicken until the centre reaches 74°C (165°F).
Lift the chicken onto a clean plate and pull it into shreds. Toss it with barbecue sauce.
Brush the bread lightly with oil and toast for a few minutes. Drain the pineapple thoroughly and cut into smaller pieces.
Top the toast with the barbecue chicken, pineapple and grated cheddar. Return to the oven for 5–7 minutes until bubbling.
Scatter over sliced spring onions and serve the open toasts immediately.

title: Chipotle chicken wraps
steps: Finely chop the chipotles. Stir half into the yoghurt with a squeeze of lime.
Cut the chicken into strips and toss with the remaining chipotle, cumin, salt and oil.
Sear in a hot skillet until browned and the centre reaches 74°C (165°F). Squeeze the rest of the lime over it.
Warm the tortillas. Chop the lettuce and drain the corn thoroughly.
Spread the yoghurt on the wraps and add lettuce, corn and chicken. Roll firmly, toast the filled wraps briefly in a dry pan and cut them in half on the diagonal.

title: Beef and sweet potato bowls with herby yoghurt
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and cut the sweet potato into small cubes.
Toss the cubes with most of the oil, half the paprika and some salt. Roast for 22–26 minutes, turning once.
Heat the remaining oil in a frying pan and break up the beef as it browns.
Season with the remaining paprika, cumin and salt and cook through. Cut the cucumber into small cubes.
Whisk the yoghurt with chopped mint, parsley and lemon juice.
Pile the sweet potato, beef and cucumber into bowls, and spoon over the herby yoghurt.

title: Malaysian creamy curry leaf chicken
steps: Rinse the rice and set it on to cook. Dice the chicken, slice the chilli and crush the garlic.
Toss the chicken in cornflour and salt. Shallow-fry in a hot pan in batches until golden and 74°C (165°F).
Drain the chicken on a rack. Melt the butter in a clean frying pan and add the garlic, curry leaves and sliced chilli.
When the leaves sizzle, stir in the evaporated milk and sugar. Simmer gently until the sauce thickens enough to lightly coat a spoon.
Tip in the crispy chicken and turn it through the sauce just before serving.
Spoon alongside rice and make sure each serving gets a few curry leaves.

title: Spinach and artichoke chicken
steps: Slice the chicken into four even cutlets. Drain and quarter the artichokes and crush the garlic.
Heat the oil in a skillet and brown the chicken on both sides. Lift it onto a clean plate.
Stir the garlic into the pan briefly and pour in the stock. Scrape up the browned bits, then stir in cream cheese.
Return the chicken along with the artichokes and simmer until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F).
Fold in spinach and grated parmesan. Let the spinach wilt, then add lemon juice and cracked pepper.
Serve the chicken with plenty of the spinach and artichoke sauce and slices of lightly toasted baguette to mop it up.

title: Sloppy Joe potato tot casserole
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Dice the onion and pepper and crush the garlic.
Brown the mince in a dry pan, breaking it up until it is cooked through.
Add the onion and pepper and soften for 5 minutes. Stir in garlic and paprika.
Add passata, ketchup and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer until the beef mixture is thick enough to mound.
Spread the beef into a baking dish. Scatter over half the grated cheese and arrange the frozen potato tots in a single layer.
Bake for 22–26 minutes until the tots are crisp and the sauce is bubbling. Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top for the final 3 minutes. Rest for a few minutes before serving.

title: Sweet paprika chicken cutlets
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Cook the rice following the packet.
Trim the beans, toss with half the oil and roast for 12–15 minutes, until browned at the tips.
Slice the chicken horizontally into thin cutlets. Rub them with paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper and the rest of the oil.
Heat a frying pan until hot and sear the cutlets on both sides until browned and 74°C (165°F) inside.
Fluff the cooked rice and fold through the butter. Squeeze lemon juice over the cooked chicken.
Serve the cutlets with the loose buttered rice and roasted beans.

title: Red curry chicken ramen with carrots
steps: Chop the chicken into bite-size pieces and slice the carrot into thin sticks. Slice the spring onions, keeping the green tops separate.
Heat the oil in a deep pan. Fry the curry paste, spring-onion whites and ginger for a minute.
Add the chicken and turn it through the paste, then pour in the coconut milk and stock.
Bring to a lively simmer. Add the carrots and cook until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F).
Drop in the ramen and cook just until the noodles are tender. Take off the heat and stir in lime juice.
Ladle into bowls and scatter over the reserved spring-onion greens.

title: Baked turkey and herb meatballs
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Rinse the rice and set it on to cook.
Mix turkey, beaten egg, breadcrumbs, crushed garlic, oregano, most of the chopped parsley and salt.
Shape into 16 small meatballs. Set on an oiled roasting tray and turn to coat lightly.
Roast for 15–19 minutes until golden and the centres reach 74°C (165°F).
Stir lemon zest, juice and a little water into the yoghurt to make a light dressing.
Serve the browned meatballs over rice with the dressing and the remaining parsley.

title: Crispy chicken tenders with wedges
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Cut the potatoes into wedges, toss with half the oil and roast for 15 minutes.
Cut the chicken into thick strips. Put flour in one bowl, beaten eggs in another and breadcrumbs mixed with paprika, garlic powder and salt in a third.
Dip the chicken first in flour, then egg and then breadcrumbs. Press the crumbs against the chicken.
Set the strips on a second lined tray and brush lightly with the remaining oil.
Turn the wedges and add the chicken tray. Bake both for 14–17 minutes, turning the chicken once, until crisp and 74°C (165°F) inside.
Serve the tenders with the wedges and ketchup for dipping.

title: Honey garlic chicken and chilli crisp noodles
steps: Cook the noodles until just tender, keeping a mug of their cooking water. Dice the chicken and cut the broccoli small.
Mix honey with crushed garlic, soy and vinegar. Thinly slice the spring onions.
Heat the oil in a frying pan and fry the chicken until golden and fully cooked to 74°C (165°F).
Stir in the broccoli and a splash of noodle water for 3 minutes.
Add the noodles and honey-garlic mixture. Toss over high heat until the sauce is glossy.
Fold through most of the chilli crisp. Spoon the rest over the bowls with sliced spring onions.

title: Nepali-style chicken curry
steps: Chop the onion and tomatoes and grate the garlic and ginger. Cut the chicken into pieces.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Add fenugreek seeds and stir just until they darken slightly.
Add the onion and cook until golden. Stir in the chicken, garlic, ginger, turmeric, coriander, cumin and salt.
Brown the chicken for a few minutes. Add the tomatoes and a splash of water, cover and simmer.
Cook until the chicken reaches 74°C (165°F) and the tomatoes form a loose gravy. Meanwhile, cook the rice following the packet.
Serve the curry with rice and chopped fresh coriander.

title: Beef and pepperoni pizza
steps: Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with a baking tray inside.
Mix flour, baking powder, salt and yoghurt into a soft dough. Knead briefly and roll into a large thin round.
Brown the beef in a frying pan until cooked through, then drain off excess fat.
Put the base on baking paper and slide onto the hot tray. Bake for 5 minutes to set the surface.
Brush with oil and spread with passata. Add oregano, torn mozzarella, cooked beef and pepperoni slices.
Bake for a further 10–14 minutes until the crust is crisp and the cheese is bubbling. Rest briefly before slicing.

title: Lemongrass beef vermicelli bowls
steps: Prepare the vermicelli following the packet and drain well. Slice the cucumber and cut the carrot into matchsticks.
Finely chop the tender lemongrass core and the garlic. Mix with half the fish sauce and rub onto the steak.
Heat the oil in a heavy pan and sear the steak on both sides to at least 63°C (145°F). Rest for at least 3 minutes.
Whisk the lime juice, sugar and remaining fish sauce with a splash of water.
Slice the steak across the grain. Divide the noodles into bowls and add the cucumber, carrots and sliced beef.
Spoon over the dressing and scatter with coriander and crushed peanuts.

title: Chilli-lime chicken and corn salad
steps: Rub thin chicken cutlets with lime zest, chilli powder, cumin, a little oil and half the salt.
Sear the chicken to 74°C (165°F) in the centre. Set it aside to rest, then slice.
Dry the corn and char it in the same pan. Chop the lettuce and tomatoes and dice the onion.
Whisk juice from two limes with the remaining oil and salt.
Toss the vegetables with the dressing and top with sliced chicken. Serve with wedges of the final lime.

title: Japanese-style tomato and egg rice bowl
steps: Rinse the rice and cook it following the packet. Cut the tomatoes into chunky wedges.
Whisk the eggs and slice the spring onions, keeping the green tops separate.
Heat the oil in a frying pan. Fry the spring-onion whites for a moment, then add the tomatoes.
Add soy sauce, vinegar and sugar. Cook just until the tomatoes start to soften.
Turn the heat low, pour the eggs over the tomatoes and fold slowly until broad soft curds form. Cook until set, then take off the heat.
Spoon the tomato-egg scramble next to the rice and finish with sliced spring-onion greens.

title: Chicken queso tortillas
steps: Gently simmer the chicken in water until the centre reaches 74°C (165°F). Let it cool slightly and shred it.
Mix grated cheddar, cream cheese, paprika, cumin and finely sliced spring onions.
Spread the queso on four tortillas, add the shredded chicken and cover with the remaining tortillas.
Toast in a dry skillet, flipping carefully once the bottom is golden. Cook until both sides are toasted and the filling is melted.
Rest for a minute, then cut each tortilla stack into wedges and serve with salsa.
